correctness.rationale: For a zero in part i, the open neighborhood is exactly the union of all other parts, so feasibility is precisely the displayed outside-part color condition. The multinomial enumerator follows from independent label counts. In a minimum function, every color absent from fully colored parts must occur in at least two distinct partially colored parts. The residual two-incidence placement is characterized exactly by a capacitated Hall inequality, and the construction attains the lower bound. Exhaustive enumeration through order seven and four colors agrees with the classification, enumerator, and minimum formula.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete feasible-function classification and weight enumerator for a canonical graph class, then solves the arbitrary-k minimum by a nontrivial capacity criterion. It is not a routine scalar special case: the Hall condition explains exactly when colors not hosted by fully colored parts can be duplicated across partial parts, and the result simultaneously covers every k, including the currently active k=3 case.
